card.name: Cibi
card.tagline: Fiji's Bauan war dance, the Flying Fijians' pre-match challenge
card.profile: The Cibi (pronounced 'thimbi') is a Fijian meke of Bauan origin, historically a war dance performed before or after battle (Wikipedia). On returning home victorious, warriors heralded their victory and were met by women singing with gestures. It came to prominence in 1939 when captain Ratu Sir George Cakobau, seeking an equivalent to the All Blacks' haka, approached Ratu Bola, high chief of the warrior clan of Navusaradave in Bau, who taught the team the Cibi; it has been the Fiji national rugby union team's pre-match ritual ever since (Wikipedia). It is also known as Teivovo after its opening chant 'Ai tei vovo'. In 2012 it was briefly replaced by the 'Bole' war cry before reverting.
card.insight: The Cibi is one of the Pacific's most recognizable sporting war dances, frequently and incorrectly conflated with the New Zealand haka; museum records (Alexander Turnbull Library) note historical photos 'previously incorrectly identified as a haka' (DigitalNZ).
